name: ClickHouse
model: Tables of typed columns, SQL; built for scanning and aggregating billions of rows; append-heavy, updates and deletes are costly
engine_note: MergeTree: sorted, compressed column parts written per insert and merged in the background (LSM-like); sparse primary index
consistency: No general transactions: one INSERT into one partition is atomic (all rows or none); multi-statement transactions are experimental, snapshot isolation, not in Cloud. Inserts not fsynced by default. Replication is async: replicas can be stale.
scaling: Shard tables across servers (manual, Distributed table) plus async multi-primary replicas coordinated by ClickHouse Keeper; ClickHouse Cloud separates compute from object storage (SharedMergeTree).
version_note: Latest LTS line is 26.8 (v26.8.17.4-lts, same day).
reach: Reach for it when you need sub-second SQL over billions of event rows (logs, metrics, product analytics) on your own servers or ClickHouse Cloud.
avoid: Avoid when you need frequent single-row updates, multi-row transactions or strict read-after-write; it is not your app's system of record.
escape: scanning billions of rows for dashboards is 10--100x faster in compressed columns than in Postgres row pages
chat: Usage events and token counts per user per minute, for dashboards and billing rollups.
notes: Licence checked: LICENSE file is Apache 2.0 (Copyright 2016-2026 ClickHouse, Inc.); its git history from 2020 to 2026-01-01 shows only copyright-year and holder edits (Sep 2021 holder changed after the spin-out from Yandex), no licence change in 2025 or 2026. Atomic-insert conditions: data fits in max_insert_block_size (about 1M rows) and goes to one partition. Durability needs fsync_after_insert or insert_quorum per docs. No Jepsen analysis exists. Other managed vendors (Altinity, Aiven, Tinybird) not verified, left out. 'LSM-like' is my description of MergeTree parts plus merges, not a docs quote.
